description.narrative: Insatsen avser ett gemensamt program mellan UNDP, UN Women och UNFPA. Programmet utgör en fortsättning på ett tidigare program som pågått från 2012 - 2015. FN organen ansvarar för implementeringen av var sin komponent och avtalet tecknas med UNDP. UN Women kommer att ha rollen som "convening agent" för att stärka koordingeringen mellan FN-organen. Fokus och mål för de olika komponenterna är som följer. UNDP ansvarar för komponent 1 som syftar till att främja kvinnors politiska och ekonomiska deltagande och omfattar bl.a. stöd till centrala MR rådet, yrkesutbildning för kvinnor och stöd till kvinnliga politiker på kommunnivå. UN Women ansvarar för komponent 2 som syftar till att skapa möjligheter att utplåna våld mot kvinnor och flickor, med särskilt fokus på sexuellt våld och våld i hemmet. Komponenten omfattar bl.a. arbete med att stärka polisens och åklagarnas arbete mot våld mot kvinnor samt stöd till ytterligare två skyddade boenden. UNFPA ansvarar för komponent 3 med målet att stärka jämställdhet och sexuella rättigheter för de mest utsatta kvinnorna, tonåringar och ungdomar. Denna komponent inkluderar bl.a. arbete med läroplanen för att inkludera sexualundervisning, stöd till ombudsmannen för uppföljning av sexuella rättigheter och påverkanskampanjer med särskilt fokus på män och rollen som pappa. Samtliga komponenter omfattar arbete på nationell, lokal och gräsrotsnivå och programmet arbetar holistiskt med policyrådgivning, stärkande av nationella system för att leverera tjänster och uppföljning och med att stärka civilsamhällets påverkan och deltagande i beslutsprocesser.

The contribution concerns a joint programming initiative between UNDP, UN Women and UNFPA, The programme is a continuation and a previous program from 2012 – 2015. The UN agencies are responsible for one component each and the agreement is signed with UNDP. UN Women will have the role as a convening agent to strengthen coordination between the UN agencies. The content and planned results of the components are as follows. UNDP is responsible for component 1 which aims at enhanced women’s political and economic empowerment and includes activities related to the Inter-Agency Human Rights Council, vocational training for women and support to women local councilors. UN Women is responsible for component 2 , which aims at creating an enabling environment to eliminate violence against women and girls, especially sexual violence and domestic violence. The component will include activities to support the work of the police and prosecutors office and the creation of two new shelters. UNFPA is responsible for component 3 with the aim to advance gender equality and reproductive rights, including for the most vulnerable women, adolescents and youth. This component includes for example work with the inclusion of sexual health information in school curriculum, support to the Public Defender’s Office to monitor sexual and reproductive rights and advocacy campaigns which a special focus on men and fatherhood. All components include activities on national local and grassroots level and will have a holistic approach working with policy advocacy, strengthening national systems and public advocacy.

The programme has the following objectives: - Enhanced women's political and economic empowerment - Enabling environment to eliminate violence against women and girls, especially sexual and domestic violence, created in Georgia. - Advanced gender equality and reproductive rights, including for the most vulnerable women, adolescents and youth.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
Phase II of the UN joint program for Gender Equality in Georgia covered the period January 2016 to June 30 2022. The UNJP contributed to further develop and capacitate the national gender equality machinery, such as the permanent Parliamentary Gender Equality Council (GEC), InterAgency Commission for Gender Equality (CGE) and the Public Defenders Office (PDO). Apart from the above mentioned entities, UNJP supported several state institutions at the legislative and executive branches to enhance capacity on gender mainstreaming, adopt and implement gender equality action plans, including contributed to the government adopting gender equality chapters of the National Human Rights Action Plans.
The UNJP have supported the Gender Equality Department of the Public Defener's Office.
UNJP has also supported the work to carry out regular monitoring of the state run shelters in Georgia and to revise and update the monitoring methodology of the state shelters, crisis centers and hotlines for the victims of domestic violence.
Support to the LGBTQI community
UNJP has also supported the Public Defender's Office in developing the first special report on the human rights situation of the LGBTQI community in Georgia. This will also strengthen the capacity of the Public Defender's Office to monitor implementation of the legislation around domestic violence.
Furthermore, the first ever policy document on enhancing LGBTQI rights in Georgia and address hate crimes against LGBTQI was in 2019 included as a chapter of the National Human Rights Action Plan on Enhancement of the Equality Policy and Combating Discrimination.
Violence against Women in Politics
The advocacy and awareness raising work enabled the UNJP to launch the first ever study on Violence against Women in Politics in Georgia completed in 2021. The study provided needed evidence and data to work towards eliminating the violence faced by many women while exercising their active and passive political rights.
Support to local communities
During phase II, UNJP increased its engagement with local municipalities across Georgia, particularly focusing on Kakheti and Samegrelo regions. As a result, the capacities of local governments to develop and implement gender equality policies have strengthened, including using tools such as gender responsible budgeting.
With UNJP support, cooperation between local municipalities and community organizations has strengthened, resulting in the allocation of 9.2 million GEL for joint projects in local budgets. Throughout the project period UNJP contributed to creating gender-sensitive local self-government through several initiatives.
Women's Economic Empowerment
In the area of Women's Economic Empowerment (WEE), the multiyear advocacy efforts to develop a state vision of WEE resulted in the first ever National Concept for Women's Economic Empowerment in 2022. UNJP also introduced the concept of care economy to Georgia and advocated for the introduction of gender-sensitive economic policies in the country.
At the local level, UNJP advocated for the launch of tailored municipal programmes for women's economic development. As a result, six municipalities have established such programmes. UNJP provided systemic support to equip the women workforce with income-generating skills, including through tailored professional education programmes. As a result of UNJP's advocacy efforts, state institutions took over UNJP-proposed professional education programmes and introduced gender equality, diversity, and inclusion among priorities.
UNJP also contributed to the vocational education reform in Georgia, with technical support directed at enhancing the diversity and inclusion components of the reform.
The UNJP, further supported the elaboration of gender-sensitive Family Policies in support of women's economic empowerment and advocated for the introduction of the new regulation for maternity, paternity, and parental leaves. Although falling short of some of the advocacy points put forward by the UNJP, the reformed Labour Code entitles fathers to take a leave for childcare for the first time.
Gender Based Violence
In terms of genderbased violence (GBV), the UNJP with the lead of UN women have continued its work on violence against women (VAW), domestic violence (DV) including sexual violence. In 2017, Georgia ratified the Istanbul Convention and adopted a milestone legal framework which was the starting point to harmonizing the domestic legislation with the requirements of the Convention, supported by UNJP.
As a result of several waves of legislative reform that have have been supported and facilitated by the UNJP, the legislation is today largely compliant with the international standards, even though some gaps remain. As a result of UNJP's support, only specialized prosecutors are now dealing with domestic violence and sexual violence cases. The nationwide hotline and five crisis centres established by support from UNJP are now fully funded by the state. Today 18 percent of women who have experienced intimate partner violence have appealed for support to the police, as opposed to only 1.5 per cent in 2009.
Sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR)
In terms of UNJP's work on sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) led by UNFPA, the UNJP managed to advance harmful practices and women and girls SRHR on the political agenda and accelerate action in response to the commitments assumed at the Nairobi Summit of ICPD25.
UNJP supported the Government of Georgia to follow up on its international commitments related to SRHR. The country accepted 69 out of 70 SRHR-related recommendations raised during Georgias second review of the Universal Periodic Report. During the third periodic review in 2021, the country adopted 257 recommendations out of 285, which is 34.55% increase with respect to the 2nd cycle.
The UNJP further introduced legislative amendments to create a better regulatory framework for combating harmful practices of Early/Child Marriage. As result, the Civil Code of Georgia was amended to strictly determine the legal age of marriages without any exception. The Criminal Code of Georgia was amended to criminalize sexual intercourse of an adult with a minor under 16, as well as forced marriages.
Comprehensive Sexuality Education
The UNJP also further strengthened the National Curriculum of Georgia by integrating various topics of Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) in the formal education system. The national curriculum is relatively well loaded with topics from CSE on the basic education level, while primary education and secondary education levels still need to ensure the provision of age-relevant education.
UNJP also invested in improving the quality of the school textbooks in Biology and Civic Education, provided technical assistance to the Ministry of Education and Science to train the master trainers of biology and civic education (78 in total) on CSE. In cooperation with the local Education Resource Centers, Memorandum of Understandings were concluded with 4 schools in Kakheti and 10 schools in Samegrelo to carry out peer education training sessions. In total, UNJP reached 5,861 young people through peer education training sessions in Kakheti and Samegrelo regions, and 941 pupils through schoolbased peer education.
Specific efforts have been made by UNJP to address needs and improve protection of rights of LGBTQI persons. To further enhance equality, diversity and equality mechanisms, during the global pandemic, UNDP partnered with the Administration of the Government to establish a Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) for LGBTQI communities responding to the most urgent socio-economic needs.
During the final year of the reporting period, the cooperation with LGBTQI community organizations resulted in the semiformal coordination mechanism - Task Force on LGBTQI rights. UNJP, with UNDP as lead, further coordinated efforts of diplomatic core and donors to address LGBTQI rights challenges in Georgia, including the annual statement on IDAHOBIT.
During phase II, UNJP increased efforts to strengthen Georgia's civil society with a focus on women's rights organisations and community organizations working on gender equality and women's empowerment in different ways, including LGBTQI community organizations. This was done by introducing communitycentred approaches, capacity building and advocacy initiatives to empower rights holders. The efforts have strengthened CSOs at the national and local levels who continuously advocate for issues of gender equality, diversity, and social inclusion.
UNJPs work have also been aimed to increase awareness, change attitudes, challenge stereotypes and increase mens involvement under each of the sub-thematic areas. This has been done through research and publication of reports and evidence, information campaigns, training of journalists etc.
